data.body:
Closed obsolete. Evidence for the criteria, recorded here rather than in the description on purpose.

AC1 — the live MCP write surface was driven end to end:
create / show / search / list / comment / edit / link / unlink / claim / transition / reopen.

AC2 — the anomalies it surfaced are filed as separate tickets, linked `relates_to` from this
probe: `1eb6-65f2-5a4e-4c7b` (attested-source LLM gates unusable on the deployed server — the
substantive find, now fixed by Gerrit 2271) and `5a38-ad96-2e09-4904`.

WHY THIS EVIDENCE IS IN A COMMENT. I first wrote it INTO the description alongside the ticks,
which turned a certified plan-review attestation `stale-material`: the gate reported
'description (960 -> 1232 chars); its TEXT changed, and checkbox state changed too (0 -> 4
ticked), which is NOT the cause; ticking an AC checkbox is attestation-SAFE'. Reverting to pure
ticks restored `certified` immediately and the close proceeded with no new LLM run. Worth knowing
for anyone closing a gated ticket: tick the boxes, put the evidence in a comment, and you keep
the attestation — add prose to the description and you buy yourself a fresh 15-20 minute
billable review for nothing.
